text:
Evan Rodrigues won two Stanley Cups in Florida and is now giving the Devils exactly what a two-time champion is supposed to bring: five goals and two assists in a six-game run through Nov. 25, a power-play goal against Columbus, and a lot of hockey sense, as The Hockey News put it.

The hot stretch is earned in part. Over his last ten games his own chances are worth 2.7 expected goals against a usual 2.0. But the finishing is the bigger driver: eight goals on 4.8 expected, shooting 21% after 7% last season, and our talent range expects closer to 12%. That rate rarely lasts.

Here is the twist: the luck around him runs the other way. New Jersey has scored 7.1 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which has kept his assists down. The worry is at five on five, where the Devils' share of the chances is almost eight points worse with him than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking said he shoots a lot but not always from the slot. Watch whether the shots move inside when the percentages cool.
